strings.page.flow.label: Sequence of the steps of {name}
strings.md.entities.domains.heading: Domains
strings.md.entities.domains.note: A domain is a kind of business object or a stretch of business that readers handle together; it can hold features from several areas of the map.
strings.md.entities.domains.purposesNote: What it does lists only the purposes of the features that were verified, in the words of their entries.
strings.md.entities.domains.flowNote: Each arrow sums the handoffs of entries from a feature of one domain to a feature of another, and its number says how many. Only the domains with such a handoff are drawn.
strings.md.entities.domains.flowNone: No entry hands off to a feature of another domain, so there is no flow to draw. An entry in the older format states no handoffs.
strings.md.entities.domain.flowNote: The flow of this domain is drawn from features, states and fragments of chapters. Every arrow was checked against a hand-over, a transition, the order of two items of one chapter, or a state name inside an item. What is drawn from a chapter is as unverified as the chapter.
strings.md.entities.domain.flowNone: No flow diagram was written for this domain.
strings.md.entities.domain.flowFailed: The flow diagram of this domain failed its checks and is not drawn.
strings.md.entities.domain.relationsNote: The relations between domains come only from the handoffs of entries: a handoff from a feature of one domain to a feature of another. An entry in the older format states no handoffs, so a domain whose entries are all in that format shows none.
strings.md.entities.roles.heading: Roles
strings.md.entities.roles.note: For each role, what the entries of the features in the handbook say the role can do. This is what the entries say, not a list of permissions.
strings.md.matrix.roleFeature.heading: Roles by feature
strings.md.matrix.roleFeature.note: A cell holds what the entry of the feature says the role can do. An empty cell means the entry says nothing about the role. This is not a list of permissions.
strings.md.entities.applications.heading: Applications in detail
strings.md.entities.applications.note: A feature is listed under the application in which its quoted passages fall, with the number of passages; a passage belongs to the application with the longest matching directory. The passages of the entries in the handbook are counted; for a feature that is not verified, only those of its fact sheet. This does not say that the application implements the feature.
strings.md.entities.app.featuresHeading: Features whose quoted passages fall in this application
strings.md.entities.app.domainsHeading: Domains whose features have quoted passages in this application
strings.md.entities.app.jobsHeading: Scheduled jobs registered in files of this application
strings.md.entities.app.shownHeading: External systems that list this application as a caller, in the quoted code
strings.md.entities.app.namedHeading: External systems whose name appears in the source of this application
strings.md.entities.unattributed.heading: Quoted passages in no application
strings.md.entities.unattributed.note: Passages of the entries in the handbook that fall in no application directory. They are counted here so that none is dropped.
strings.md.entities.systems.heading: External systems in detail
strings.md.entities.systems.note: Called by, in the quoted code: the applications the system overview lists for the system, each checked against its quoted passages. Applications whose source contains the name: found by the script in the source files of each application, the name as written (same capitals), in code or in a comment. That says the name appears there, not that the application calls the system. Test files and skipped directories are not searched.
strings.md.entities.systems.diagramHeading: Applications and the external systems they call
strings.md.entities.systems.diagramNote: Each arrow is an application that the system overview shows calling an external system. Calls between applications are not drawn: the facts hold none.
strings.md.entities.systems.diagramNone: The system overview shows no application calling an external system, so there is nothing to draw.
strings.md.architecture.unverified: Not verified: this chapter and its diagram were written from the code and configuration, and no verifier or tracer has checked them.
strings.md.architecture.diagramNote: The components are placed in layers from left to right by what they are. Each component and each connection cites a passage copied from a project file; the diagram is as unverified as the chapter.
strings.md.architecture.notSelected: The architecture chapter was not written in this run; the diagram below shows only the calls to external systems that the system overview names.
strings.md.architecture.failed: The architecture chapter did not pass its checks; the diagram below shows only the calls to external systems that the system overview names.
strings.md.architecture.missing: A file of the architecture chapter is missing; the diagram below shows only the calls to external systems that the system overview names.
strings.md.entities.system.named: Applications whose source contains the name
strings.md.entities.system.namedOutside: Source files outside every listed application that contain the name: {count}.
strings.md.matrix.applicationDomain.heading: Applications by domain
strings.md.matrix.applicationDomain.note: A cell is the number of quoted passages of the domain's verified features that fall in the application. An empty cell means none.
strings.md.locations.heading: Source locations
strings.md.locations.note: For each item, the file and the lines of each passage quoted for it.
strings.md.locations.overviewHeading: Source locations of the system overview
strings.md.data.heading: Data
strings.md.data.note.nameRules: A table name appears in an application when, in a file of that application outside the migration directories, (a) a string is exactly the table name; (b) the table name comes right after FROM, JOIN, INTO, UPDATE or TABLE, or after TABLE, an opening parenthesis and a quote; or (c) the table name comes right after many2many:.
strings.md.data.note.comments: A name inside a comment counts as appearing.
strings.md.data.note.ormDefaults: Access through a model type, through a name put together from several strings, or through a library default such as the default table of an adapter, is not seen.
strings.md.data.note.onlyInMigrationsAnyRule: A name that appears only in migrations means none of these rules found it anywhere else. It does not mean the table is unused.
strings.md.data.recognized: Forms of table declaration recognized in this version: {forms}.
strings.md.data.form.migrationCalls: table calls in migration scripts (create, drop, rename and change calls with a literal table name)
strings.md.data.form.migrationSql: SQL statements in migration scripts and in .sql migration files
strings.md.data.form.goTableName: the TableName method of a Go model
strings.md.data.form.jsTableName: the tableName property of a JavaScript or TypeScript model
strings.md.data.form.sqlFileCreateTable: CREATE TABLE in .sql files outside the migration directories
strings.md.data.countLine: Tables: {tables}. Migrations: {migrations} ({replayed} replayed, {unsplit} not split, {downOnly} down only). Tables whose name appears in two or more applications: {several}. Tables whose name appears only in migrations: {onlyInMigrations}. Tables dropped by a migration: {dropped}. Tables declared by a model or a .sql file and created by no migration: {declaredOnly}. Tables removed by a migration and still declared: {removedButDeclared}. Tables changed by a migration and created by none: {changedNeverCreated}. Gaps: {gaps}.
strings.md.data.removedButDeclaredHeading: Removed by a migration (dropped or renamed away) and still declared by a model or a .sql file
strings.md.data.declaredOnlyHeading: Tables declared by a model or a .sql file and created by no migration
strings.md.data.changedNeverCreatedHeading: Tables a migration changes and no migration creates
strings.md.data.onlyInMigrationsHeading: Tables whose name appears only in migrations
strings.md.data.gap.unnamedHeading: Migration operations whose table name is not a literal
strings.md.data.gap.unsplitHeading: Migration files whose up and down parts could not be told apart

strings.md.dict.heading: Status dictionary
strings.md.dict.note.nameRule: A JavaScript object, and a TypeScript object that ends in as const, is read as a value set only when the name it is assigned to ends in Status, State, Type, Kind, Stage, Phase, Level, Role, Mode or Category, or in the plural of one of these (such as Levels or Categories), in any case. A value set with another name is not seen.
strings.md.dict.note.sources: The meaning of a value comes only from the code: the comment next to it, copied as written, and its display names, each with its place. A display name is an entry of a mapping table that has the member as its key, or, for a member whose value is an object, a message, label, name, desc or description of that object. Nothing is written by a model. A blank meaning means the code has none.
strings.md.dict.note.values: A value marked not computed is written as in the code (it refers to another constant or is an expression that was not worked out) and is not compared with the other side.
strings.md.dict.recognized: Forms of value set recognized in this version: {forms}.
strings.md.dict.form.goNamedType: Go named types declared as a string or an integer type (also in the alias form), with the constants of the same directory that are declared with that type
strings.md.dict.form.goTypedVar: Go variables declared with such a type and a value (var X T = value); a literal is the value, another expression is shown as written and marked not computed
strings.md.dict.form.tsEnum: TypeScript enum and const enum declarations
strings.md.dict.form.tsConstObject: TypeScript objects that end in as const
strings.md.dict.form.jsObject: JavaScript objects assigned to a const, let or var, to module.exports.X or to exports.X
strings.md.dict.form.jsRecordMember: members of such objects whose value is an object with a literal code, value or id (the first found, in that order), which is the value; the first string literal among message, label, name, desc and description is the display name
strings.md.dict.countLine: Value sets: {total} ({goType} Go types, {tsEnum} TS enums, {tsConstObject} TS const objects, {jsObject} JS objects). Members: {members} ({computed} computed, {notComputed} not computed). Comments: {comments}. Display names: {labels}. Same names with different values: {mismatches}. Skipped members: {skipped}.
strings.md.dict.countLineNotTaken: Candidates that are not value sets: {noConstants} Go types without constants or variables, {duplicate} Go types declared again, {untypedIota} untyped iota constants, {otherType} constants of another type, {plain} plain constants, {otherVar} variables of another type, {tsNoLiteral} TS const objects without literal members, {jsNoLiteral} JS objects without literal members. Mapping table entries that name no member: {unmatchedKey}. Mapping table entries that name more than one member: {ambiguousKey}.
strings.md.dict.mismatchNote: Value sets with the same name in two applications (ignoring case and underscores) are compared by value, not by member name.
strings.md.dict.mismatch.notCompared: Not compared, value not computed in {side}: {members}
strings.md.dict.byApplicationHeading: Value sets by application and file
strings.md.dict.set.tsConstObject: TypeScript object ending in as const, declared at {place}.
strings.md.dict.set.skipped: Parts of the declaration that were not read as members: {count}.

strings.md.dict.malformed: dictionaries.json is malformed, so the status dictionary is not shown.

strings.md.findings.heading: Findings
strings.md.findings.note: Each finding states what the code does today that is a defect, and when it happens. The findings that a verification step removed are in the coverage section.
strings.md.findings.unverifiedFeature: Not verified: these findings were written from the code, and no verifier or tracer has checked them.
strings.md.findings.unverifiedSystem: Not verified: these system findings were written from the code, and no verifier or tracer has checked them.

strings.md.history.heading: Code health
strings.md.history.note: A script counts these numbers from the version history and the project files. They describe the history as it is.
strings.md.history.notWritten: The code health section was not written for this handbook.
strings.md.history.malformed: The code health file is not in the format this version reads.
strings.md.history.noHistory: There is no version history to count: {reason}. The test files below are counted from the project files.
strings.md.history.reason.notARepository: the project directory is not in a git repository
strings.md.history.reason.insideRepository: the project directory is inside a git repository that it is not the root of
strings.md.history.reason.noCommits: the repository has no commit under the directory
strings.md.history.yearsNote: The year is the year of the author time of each commit, in UTC. The Commits column counts each commit once; a commit that changes two applications is counted in each of them in the By application column.
strings.md.history.chartNote: The chart is drawn by a script from the table above.
strings.md.history.appsNote: Commits are counted without merges, in the directory of the application. Authors are the distinct author emails. The last column is the fewest authors, most commits first, whose commits make up at least 80% of the commits of the application.
strings.md.history.hotspotsNote: The score of a file is its number of commits times its number of lines at the latest commit. The 15 files with the highest score are listed. The features are the verified entries that quote a passage of the file. Git may not follow a file through a rename, so the history of a renamed file can start at the rename.
strings.md.history.uncertainNote: A count marked uncertain is for a file whose history branches: at that many commits git could not tell which file of the same name was changed, so the count can leave out or include those commits.
strings.md.history.coChangeNote: Two files are a pair when the same commits change both. A pair is listed only when its two files are in different applications, the pair was changed together in at least 3 commits, and a commit that changes more than 30 files is not counted. The 10 pairs with the most commits are listed.
strings.md.history.testsNote: A test file is a file in a source language whose name follows one of these conventions: {conventions}. A test that follows none of them is not counted. A source file is a file in a source language that is not a test file.
strings.md.appendix.heading: Appendix
strings.md.appendix.note: A script writes the appendix from the entries and the records of this run. It adds no statement of its own.
strings.md.appendix.openNote: Each item is one thing that an entry or the system overview says it did not find, in its own words, with the places it searched.
strings.md.appendix.table.question: Question
strings.md.appendix.glossaryNote: Each term is written as the entries write it, once. Terms that differ in case or spacing are separate terms. The terms are in the order of their Unicode code points.
strings.md.appendix.read: This handbook is written from the source files of the project and its version history.
strings.md.appendix.notRead: It does not use the deployment configuration, the production data or what the system does while it runs.
strings.md.appendix.checks: Each part of this handbook that a model wrote was written once by a subagent from the code. Scripts then checked it: every quoted passage exists in its source file, the shape, the numbers, the labels and the words of reader text. No verifier, tracer or judge reads a part after that, and a part written this way is marked as not verified. An item that did not pass a script check is not in this handbook.
strings.md.appendix.sectionsNote: Items kept are the items of the verified units that quote a passage; a unit that is written and not verified keeps no count here. Removed by the verifiers and removed by the tracers count the records an older run left of items taken out of the units. Written again counts the units whose lane ran more than once, one for each run after the first.
strings.md.appendix.rankedNote: Kept is what is in this handbook; left out is what the judges did not both accept, or, for the levels, the groups of findings that have none.
strings.md.appendix.ranked.priority: Levels of the groups of findings
